sections.title: Survival Actions Keyword
sections.text:
Remember the keyword SURVIVAL:
S - Size Up the Situation (Size up your surroundings, your physical condition, and your equipment).
U - Use All Your Senses, Undue Haste Makes Waste (Quick movements without thinking can lead to capture or injury).
R - Remember Where You Are (Always maintain your bearings on a map or mental grid).
V - Vanquish Fear and Panic (Panic is the greatest enemy in a survival crisis).
I - Improvise (Use whatever materials are around you to meet your basic needs).
V - Value Living (Maintain the will to survive above all hardships).
A - Act Like the Natives (Observe how local fauna and indigenous peoples obtain food and water).
L - Live By Your Wits (Learn basic skills before an emergency occurs).

sections.title: Pattern for Survival
sections.text:
Develop a survival pattern that meets your basic needs in priority order:
1. First Aid — Assess yourself and companions for life-threatening injuries, bleeding, or shock.
2. Shelter — Protect yourself from harsh elements (cold, excessive heat, wind, rain).
3. Fire — Provides warmth, a means to purify water, signal rescuers, and cook food.
4. Water — The human body can survive weeks without food, but only days without water.
5. Food — Necessary for long-term energy and morale once immediate life threats are secured.

sections.title: Water Sources
sections.text:
Water is essential to life. The body loses water through perspiration, respiration, and urination. Never wait until you are out of water before searching for a source.
Look for signs of water: lush vegetation, swarms of insects, animal tracks converging toward low ground, bird flight paths at dawn and dusk. In mountainous terrain, dig in dry stream beds where gravel is moist.

sections.title: Water Purification Methods
sections.text:
Always purify water before drinking unless obtained directly from a clean spring or rain catchment.
1. Boiling: The most certain method. Bring water to a rolling boil for at least 1 full minute (3 minutes at high altitudes over 2,000 meters) to kill all pathogenic bacteria, viruses, and parasites.
2. Chemical Treatment: Use water purification tablets (iodine or chlorine) according to directions, or 2 drops of 5% household bleach per liter of clear water, letting it stand for 30 minutes.
3. Filtration: Pass turbid water through a layered filter of clean sand, crushed charcoal from your campfire, and fine cloth before boiling to remove suspended particulate matter.

sections.title: Basic Fire Principles
sections.text:
To start and sustain a fire, you require three elements: heat, fuel, and oxygen.
Gather three grades of fuel before lighting:
1. Tinder: Fine, bone-dry material that ignites with a single spark (dry birch bark, shredded cedar inner bark, dry lint, charred cotton cloth, crushed dry grass).
2. Kindling: Small dry twigs and split sticks from pencil-lead to thumb thickness.
3. Fuel: Larger dry logs and hardwoods that provide long-lasting heat and sustained coals.
